$comment: How a client holds a session, as every SDK must compute it. `refreshSchedule`: how long to wait before renewing an access token, from its own claims. The margin before expiry is half the token's lifetime (`exp - iat`, or the time remaining when there is no `iat`), capped at 300 seconds; the wait is never under 10 seconds; a token with no readable `exp` schedules nothing (`delay` null). Times are in seconds; a row gives the token's `claims`, which a runner puts in any JWT, or a literal `token`. `tokenExpiry`: reading `exp` out of a token. A JWT's segments are base64url without padding, and its payload is UTF-8, so a reader that assumes plain base64 or ASCII fails for the accounts whose names produce `-`, `_` or a multi-byte character. `startup`: what a session does with the credential it finds stored, when it starts. It asks the gateway who the token is. A token the gateway refuses is renewed at the issuer once and asked about once more; a token the issuer has just issued and the gateway refuses is final, because renewing again cannot change the answer, and the session ends as `session.credential-refused`. So a session asks at most twice and renews at most once, whatever the gateway and the issuer answer. A row scripts both: `stored` is the access token found (`unexpired`, `expired`, or `none`), `gateway` what the gateway answers each time it is asked (`accepts`, `refuses`: a 401, `unreachable`: no usable answer) and `issuer` what the issuer answers each renewal (`renews`, `refuses`); the last answer of each repeats, so a runner must fail a session that asks more than `asks` times or renews more than `renewals`. `ends` is `signed-in` (a token, and who it is), `signed-out` (neither) or `unconfirmed` (a token, and nobody to say who it is). A session that ends `signed-out` asks neither of them anything afterwards, however long it is held. `told` is the reason a session gives `onAuthFailed` when it ends, `expired` (its token could not be renewed) or `refused` (the gateway refused a token its issuer had just issued), and `error` the code reported, each null when there is none. A reason is not a sentence: what a person reads is the host's to say, in their language; `kept` is whether a session is still stored. `refusal`: what a session that is already running does when the gateway refuses its token, which is when its transport asks it to `refresh`. The rule is the one `startup` has: the token is renewed once and the gateway is asked who the new one is, and a token the issuer has just issued and the gateway refuses ends the session as `session.credential-refused`. So one refusal costs at most one renewal and one ask. A row's session started signed in, on a stored token the gateway accepted; `issuer` is what the issuer answers the renewal and `gateway` what the gateway answers when asked who the renewed token is, each as in `startup`. `asks` and `renewals` count from the refusal on, and `given` is whether `refresh` gives a token. A gateway that cannot be asked refuses nothing: the renewed token is given, and nothing is said. A renewal the session makes on its own schedule follows no refusal, and asks nobody. TypeScript runs this in packages/sdk (session-agreement.test.ts), Rust in packages/sdk-rust (tests/session_cases.rs for `refreshSchedule` and `tokenExpiry`, tests/session.rs for `startup` and `refusal`), and Python in packages/sdk-python (tests/test_session_tables.py for `refreshSchedule` and `tokenExpiry`, tests/test_session.py for `startup` and `refusal`). The launcher's Go holds a session too (oauth.go, session.go) and does not run this table.

refreshSchedule.why: an hour-long token just issued is renewed 300 seconds before it expires: the margin's ceiling
a five-minute token is renewed at half its life, not at once: a fixed 300-second margin equals this lifetime and schedules a renewal for the moment of issue, forever
a one-minute token is renewed at half its life
a ten-minute token sits where half its life equals the ceiling
the margin comes from the lifetime the issuer chose, not from what remains of it
a token past its renewal point waits the floor, never zero
an expired token waits the floor: one attempt per interval, not a loop
a token shorter than twice the floor waits the floor, though that is past its half-life
with no iat the lifetime is what remains, and half of it is still bounded
with no iat and a long time remaining the ceiling applies
a token with no exp schedules nothing
a token that is not a JWT schedules nothing

tokenExpiry.why: an ASCII payload, whose length is not a multiple of four: JWTs omit the padding
a payload whose base64url spelling contains `_`: the name is Zoë Fauré
a payload whose base64url spelling contains `-`: the name is O’Connor, with a typographic apostrophe
two segments are not a JWT
a payload that is not base64url
a payload that is not JSON

startup.why: nothing stored: nobody is asked, and nothing is said
a stored token the gateway accepts is the session's
a token the gateway refuses is renewed once and asked about again
a token the gateway refuses and the issuer will not renew: the session has expired
the gateway refuses every token the issuer goes on issuing: asked twice, renewed once, and over
a stored token that has expired is renewed before anyone is asked
an expired token the issuer will not renew is forgotten, and nothing is said: there was no session to end
an expired token is renewed and the gateway refuses the new one: it was just issued, so it is not renewed again
a gateway that cannot be asked refuses nothing: the token is kept, and the failure is said
the renewed token could not be asked about: it is kept, and the failure is said

refusal.why: the gateway accepts the renewed token: the session goes on, and the request can be made again
the gateway refuses the renewed token too: it was just issued, so the session is over
the issuer will not renew: the session has expired, and nobody is asked
a gateway that cannot be asked refuses nothing: the renewed token is given, and nothing is said
